articles.title: Wires, Boards, and a lot of Curiosity: Mentoring at India’s AI Hardware Buildathon
articles.summary: Participants in India's AI Hardware Buildathon created various edge AI projects, including a workout counter, chess board, fruit quality monitor, and HVAC system that adjust temperature based on occupancy. This showcases the potential of edge AI in real-world applications.

articles.title: How Our Research Team Developed a More Efficient Audio Embedding Model
articles.summary: The Edge Impulse team developed a smaller, open-data-trained audio embedding model for real-world sound classification and anomaly detection. This model is more efficient for edge devices, enabling real-time processing of audio data.

articles.summary: Hugging Face and Sysdig reported autonomous AI-driven intrusions, highlighting the growing threat of AI-powered attacks and the need for improved defenses.

articles.summary: A humanoid robot uses Edge Impulse and ROS 2 for on-device ball tracking and autonomous movement. This matters because it demonstrates the potential for real-time AI on edge devices in robotics applications.

articles.summary: A wearable device uses TinyML to recognize hand gestures, enabling patients to communicate quickly and privately. This technology matters because it provides a new way for patients to interact with their environment without relying on verbal communication.
